text:
New Jersey needed overtime to beat Detroit, and the Devils needed it only because the game stayed closer than the way they played it. Jack Hughes ended it 1:19 into the extra period, a snap shot set up by Jesper Bratt, and the numbers say that was a fair outcome: New Jersey generated 4.51 expected goals to Detroit's 2.25, and in simulated replays of every shot the Devils win 83 percent of the time.

The gap opened early. New Jersey carried a 1.83 to 0.26 edge in chance quality through the first period, yet Emmitt Finnie tied it at 1-1 with a wrist shot late in the period, a goal worth just a 6 percent chance. Detroit pushed ahead in the second when Michael Brandsegg-Nygård scored 1:43 in, but New Jersey answered three times in that period. Anthony Mantha tied it on a 2 percent chance, Nico Hischier tipped in a power-play goal, and Bratt made it 4-3 late. Alex DeBrincat had pulled Detroit even in between, also on a 2 percent chance.

Hughes was the driver, with eight shots, 1.57 individual expected goals and a goal and two assists. DeBrincat kept Detroit alive with two goals, the second tying it 4-4 in the third on a 6 percent chance, after Detroit finally edged the period 0.80 to 0.49 in chance quality. Neither goalie stole anything: Jake Allen allowed 1.75 more goals than expected and John Gibson 0.49 more. Detroit's 25 hits to New Jersey's 13 never turned into territory, and the Devils took the extra point they had earned over the full 60 minutes.
